transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-30
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Alex Gomez (Redwood), Tom Erickson (SchedulerHealth CTO), Maya Lopez (Head of MLOps), Samir Khan (Security), Lena Park (PM)

--- Summary (auto) ---
Jordan: quick intro; Priya demoed model catalog and console; we walked through benchmarks and compat matrix; discussed hosting options and security; agreed next steps.

--- Transcript ---
00:00 Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood, and with me is Priya, our SE, and Alex from product. Tom, Maya, thanks for making the time.
00:18 Tom: Hey Jordan, thanks, excited to see the catalog. We're mainly focused on a scheduling assistant for clinics, so latency and PHI are concerns.
00:30 Jordan: Totally, we'll hit those. Quick agenda — model selection in the catalog, bench results, compatibility matrix, and how that maps to Hosted, Dedicated, and Private. Save questions as we go.
00:45 Maya: Sounds good. Also want to cover integration points with our SSO and KMS.
00:52 Priya: Great, jumping into the console — this is the model catalog view, you can filter by task, architecture, and our verified performance profiles. Note: some model names in the UI show family + profile, e.g., gpt-neox-20B (fp16) vs gpt-j-6b-8bit.
01:18 Priya: We recommend open models for visibility — you can pin versions and compare benchmarks side-by-side. For SchedulerHealth I highlighted two families that fit: a small Llama variant for low-cost, and a mid-size neoX for higher quality with similar latency after quantization.
01:42 Tom: Can you show the benchmark numbers? Our SLA target is sub-300ms p50 and sub-800ms p99 for 512 tokens.
01:52 Priya: Yep — pulling the bench tab, these results are from our standard 4k context test with continuous batching. For the neoX-20b quantized 8-bit on a V100-equivalent we see p50 ~180ms, p99 ~720ms under 20 rps; with batching tuned it improves. The small Llama-7b 8-bit is p50 ~90ms, p99 ~420ms.
02:18 Samir: Just to interrupt, those numbers assume no PHI encryption overhead and typical KV cache hit rates, right?
02:28 Priya: Correct, those are raw inference numbers. If you enable envelope encryption and KMS calls per-token, there's an added small overhead — usually low single-digit percent but depends on your KMS latency and whether you do per-request wrapping.
02:45 Tom: For high concurrency weekends, we might need Dedicated. What's the cost delta?
02:52 Jordan: Hosted is usage-based; we give you per-token and per-embed pricing. Dedicated gives predictable monthly commit and better isolation — usually 30–40% lower unit cost at scale depending on usage profile, plus reserved GPU pools for SLOs.
03:10 Maya: Any middle ground? autoscaling burst?
03:15 Jordan: Yes Dedicated supports burst capacity and configurable autoscale policies. Also can route low-latency traffic to Dedicated and fallback to Hosted if capacity is exceeded.
03:30 Lena: Walk us through the compatibility matrix — hardware, quantization, and kernel support.
03:36 Priya: Sure — here's the compatibility matrix view. It maps model families to supported quantizations (fp16, int8/4, q4_0, q8_0 in our notation), recommended kernel backend, and validated sequence lengths. Important note: some older kernels don't support q4_0 well, so the matrix flags sweet spots — e.g., neoX-20b best on A100-style with q8_0; on T4-like hardware we recommend the Llama-7b fp16 path or q4 variants.
04:06 Tom: Are those per-model recommended quant profiles validated by Redwood?
04:11 Priya: Yup — these are Redwood-verified performance profiles, we run model-specific evals and bench runs across our fleet. The matrix includes quality delta estimates compared to fp16 baseline.
04:28 Tom: There's often a quality hit with aggressive quant. How do you guard against regression?
04:33 Priya: We pair quant recommendations with eval prompt-sets. In the Optimize tab you can upload prompt sets and Redwood will run quality monitors and regression alerts tied to those prompts — helps catch regressions when swapping quant or model version.
04:48 Maya: For Private deployment, does the console look the same? We need VPC and audit logs.
04:54 Jordan: Consistent console experience across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private. Private gives you a customer-controlled control plane, KMS integration, and audit logs. You'll still see the catalog and compatibility views.
05:12 Samir: On encryption — we need HSM/KMS and audit trail for HIPAA. How mature are those integrations?
05:20 Priya: We have KMS integrations with AWS KMS and Customer-managed keys, and a certified HSM path for Private installs. Audit logs include token-level traces and per-request metadata; we can filter by user, route, and model. We'll share SOC2 and HIPAA artifacts after call.
05:40 Tom: Competitors often overstate latency; how reproducible are your bench numbers?
05:46 Priya: We publish the bench harness and the run conditions. For reproducibility we include sequence length dist, batch sizes, hardware spec, and kernel versions. We'll send our bench CSVs for the models we discussed.
06:01 Lena: Ok, concrete question — we have 4-week pilot timeline. Can we spin up a Dedicated pilot for the clinic scheduling assistant?
06:08 Jordan: Yes; typically pilot is 2–8 weeks depending on scale. We'll propose a small Dedicated pool for consistent latency and run the initial bench and integration tests.
06:18 Tom: Onboarding — what's needed from our side?
06:21 Jordan: API keys for initial Hosted calls, and for Dedicated/Private we'll need a contact for infra to set up VPC peering and KMS details. Also a pilot dataset for evaluation.
06:32 Maya: Data residency — we require EU data to stay in eu-west-1 for some clinics, is that supported?
06:37 Jordan: Yes, we support regional routing and can pin routes to eu-west-1. For Private you can deploy to your region.
06:45 Alex: Quick demo of Optimize — this is the cost/perf toolkit. It recommends batching, quant profiles, and caching parameters based on your traffic pattern. You can simulate changes and see estimated unit-cost delta.
07:01 Tom: If we apply caching, will it affect our SLAs for fresh responses?
07:07 Priya: Prefix/KV caching is workload-aware; for scheduling use cases we often cache system prompts or common completions. You can set TTLs and cache scope to ensure freshness for appointment-specific calls.
07:20 Lena: About model selection — could you walk through selecting an open model end-to-end?
07:26 Priya: Sure — select task (completion/chat), filter by latency/quality profile, pick candidate models (Llama-7b-q8, neoX-20b-q8), compare benches and quality deltas. Then create a route in Console — you can pin a model version, set rollout policy (canary %, fallback chain), and choose deployment mode (hosted/dedicated/private).
07:48 Tom: Do rollouts support A/B testing between different quant profiles?
07:52 Priya: Yes — you can do canary or A/B between model versions or quant variants and tie quality monitors to each variant.
08:05 Samir: We need the security questionnaire answered, plus an architecture diagram for Private.
08:11 Jordan: Noted — we'll attach the SOC2, HIPAA, network architecture for Private, and the security questionnaire in the follow-up.
08:20 Maya: Pricing rough ballpark for pilot?
08:23 Jordan: For small Dedicated pilot, expect a monthly commit + usage for overages; I'll send a workbook. Ballpark per-token hosted vs unit cost on Dedicated depends on quant and batching, but expect 25–40% savings at production scale.
08:40 Lena: On the bench CSV — can you include p50/p95/p99 lines and the raw traces?
08:46 Priya: Yes, we'll include raw traces and the config: seq len distribution, batch sizes, hardware.
08:55 Tom: Any gotchas for our infra — we're on k8s with a mix of A100 and T4 instances in prod, mostly on-prem for some clinics.
09:05 Priya: That matches common patterns. For on-prem we recommend Private or Dedicated on-prem nodes; kernel selection differs by GPU — A100 favors fp16 high-throughput kernels, T4 favors quantized kernels for cost-efficiency. We'll mark those in the matrix.
09:22 Maya: Do you support model fine-tuning or adapters?
09:26 Alex: Currently model hosting supports adapters and lightweight tuning workflows we can discuss; it's separate from the pure inference runtime but integrated in the catalog for versioning.
09:36 Tomas (accidentally labeled): [laughter]
09:40 Priya: Back to compatibility matrix — I'm toggling a view to show recommended infra for each model variant and expected unit cost delta. You can export CSV.
09:56 Tom: On evaluation, how do you measure hallucination or safety for medical content?
10:01 Priya: We run domain-specific evals with prompt sets and include safety checks; Recommend adding your clinical prompt set to Optimize and enabling regression alerts.
10:12 Samir: On SSO, we use Okta. Any issues?
10:16 Jordan: Okta SAML/SCIM supported for Hosted and Dedicated; for Private we can integrate with your IdP in the VPC.
10:24 Maya: Could you show the API example for calling a pinned model?
10:28 Priya: Sure — example curl: POST to /v1/generate with model: "redwood/neoX-20b-q8-verified" and you can set route headers to prefer Dedicated. We'll paste examples.
10:46 Tom: A few concerns from procurement: legal terms for PHI, indemnity, and data retention — can you send standard clauses?
10:55 Jordan: Yes, legal will share standard enterprise terms and HIPAA addendum.
11:05 Lena: If we go Dedicated, what's the expected latency improvement in practice?
11:09 Priya: Dedicated reduces noisy neighbor variance and gives reserved pools — expect improvements on p99 by about 10–25% over shared Hosted depending on burst profile.
11:21 Tom: Can you run a micro-bench with our sample prompt set?
11:26 Priya: Yes — preferred approach: you give us an anonymized sample, we run bench and quality eval and return results. We'll need your approval for sample data.
11:40 Samir: Security: are logs redacted by default?
11:44 Priya: We can configure redaction rules on Private and Dedicated; Hosted can also do token-level redactions per route. We'll note default retention policies and options.
11:58 Jordan: We're about halfway through, any other big questions?
12:03 Tom: No, just timeline — pilot in two weeks?
12:06 Jordan: We'll propose dates in the follow-up, pilot kickoff typically within 1–2 weeks after SOW signoff.
12:15 Maya: One last ask — include A100 vs T4 perf profiles in the compat export.
12:20 Priya: Will do, export will have per-hardware columns.
12:28 Jordan: OK briefly recapping next steps — Jordan to send pricing workbook and legal docs, Priya to share bench CSVs, compat matrix, and a micro-bench schedule, SchedulerHealth to confirm dataset and security contacts.
12:42 Tom: Thanks, this was helpful.
12:45 Jordan: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts.
12:50 Meeting end

--- End of transcript ---
